findings.title: TestLogger.FromContext returns a fresh logger, so recorded calls are lost
findings.body: `TestLogger.FromContext` returns `NewTestLogger()`, which is a new, empty instance. The only caller I found, `LoggerMiddleware.logRequest` (`logger_middleware.go:58`), now logs through `m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info(...)`. A test that injects a `*TestLogger` into `NewLoggerMiddleware` and checks `InfoLogs` on that instance will see zero calls and a nil `Ctx`. No such test exists today, and `logger_middleware.go` has no test file. Returning `f` would keep the fake usable for that kind of assertion. `New` has the same property, but `New` is not on the new request-logging path.

findings.title: New ContextualLoggerMiddleware and the FromContext-based logging have no tests
findings.body: The logic that adds the `endpoint`, `pluginId`, `dsName`, `dsUID` and `uname` attributes moved from the metrics middleware into this new file, and `LoggerMiddleware` now relies on it. Nothing in the diff tests the new middleware, and nothing checks that the "Plugin Request Completed" log still carries those fields and `traceID`. `metrics_middleware_test.go` only had its constructor name changed. A small test would cover this. It would apply the middleware, call `log.FromContext` or the logger's `FromContext` in the next client, and check the attributes. A second case would cover a request with a nil `User` and nil `DataSourceInstanceSettings`.

findings.title: Fallback branch in FromContext silently drops the context
findings.body: `ConcreteLogger.FromContext` (`pkg/infra/log/log.go:203-217`) returns either `cl` or `cl.New(args...)`, and both are `*ConcreteLogger`. The type assertion at line 49 therefore always succeeds today. The `!ok` branch returns `d.New()`, which discards both the context attributes and `traceID` without any signal. If `FromContext` ever returns another `Logger` implementation, the "Plugin Request Completed" lines would lose `pluginId`, `endpoint` and `traceID` with no error. Returning `d` as the fallback would keep the wrapper's own logger context. It would also be worth a comment saying why the assertion exists.

contracts.action: Plugin context attributes (endpoint, pluginId, dsName, dsUID, uname) are now added to the request context by a separate ContextualLoggerMiddleware instead of inside the metrics middleware's instrumentPluginRequest
contracts.equivalent_path: The removed `instrumentContext` call inside `MetricsMiddleware.instrumentPluginRequest`. It ran only after `pluginTarget` succeeded, and only for QueryData, CallResource, CheckHealth and CollectMetrics.
contracts.before_after: Before: the attributes were added after the plugin registry lookup and before `fn(ctx)`. Now: they are added unconditionally for the same four endpoints. The middleware sits after Metrics and before Logger in `pluginsintegration.go:158-161`, so every downstream middleware and the plugin client still receive the enriched context. The only difference is that an unregistered plugin now has the attributes attached before the metrics layer's `ErrPluginNotRegistered` error, which skips the inner chain anyway, so nothing observable changes. Stream methods pass through unchanged, as before.
contracts.visible_effect: Log lines emitted downstream via `FromContext` still carry the same plugin attributes.
contracts.failure_mode: The new middleware dereferences `req.PluginContext` without a nil check. The metrics middleware, placed before it, already dereferences `req` (`req.Queries`, `req.PluginContext`), so no new panic path appears. Nothing here is async.

contracts.action: LoggerMiddleware now logs via m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info and no longer adds pluginId, endpoint, uname, traceID, dsName and dsUID itself
contracts.equivalent_path: Other `log.Logger.FromContext` callers such as `pkg/api/pluginproxy/ds_proxy.go:117`. `ConcreteLogger.FromContext` merges the attributes from every registered contextual log provider.
contracts.before_after: Before: the middleware built the attributes by hand, including `tracing.TraceIDFromContext`. Now: the `WithContextualAttributes` provider (`log.go:55`) supplies the plugin attributes, and the tracing provider registered in `tracing.ProvideService` (`tracing.go:91-97`) supplies `traceID`. The tracing middleware is first in the chain, so a span is already on the context. The plugin wrapper's `FromContext` asserts `*log.ConcreteLogger`, which `ConcreteLogger.FromContext` always returns. The `uname` and `dsName` attributes now come from the context provider, which only ever gets the same values the old code used.
contracts.visible_effect: The log line keeps the same fields. The order of the keys changes, with context attributes first.
contracts.failure_mode: If `tracing.ProvideService` was never called, as in some tests, `traceID` is no longer logged. Production wiring calls it. The type-assertion fallback `d.New()` would silently drop context, but it is unreachable today.

summary: The refactor looks behavior-preserving. The context attributes move to a new middleware that runs before the logger middleware. The logger middleware reads them back through `FromContext`, and `traceID` still comes from the tracing log provider. I found nothing that blocks the merge. Three smaller points: `TestLogger.FromContext` returns a fresh logger and so loses the calls it records; the new middleware and the log-field behavior have no tests; and the wrapper's `FromContext` fallback silently drops context if its type assertion ever fails.
